feature: Generic WebExtension runtime, popup rendering and Cat Catch compatibility
status: Core workflows verified; not full Chrome API or full Cat Catch certification
changes: Retain native API wrapper owners and bind i18n methods so detached and Proxy calls remain translated across script loads and later interactions.
Keep the publisher HTML/CSS and explicitly apply the app appearance to the native popup host.

Present the official action.popupWebView in a shared bounded UIKit container. Preserve publisher HTML/CSS and native popup API identity; avoid intrinsic-size clipping of fixed controls. No publisher-specific CSS patch is shipped.

Preserve native WKUIDelegate callbacks while supporting window.close, owner-specific dismissal, fresh documents on reopen, duplicate action requests and interactive dismissal. Restore the native delegate on close.

Conservatively prepare classic workers with initial literal imports as event pages; preserve import order, package boundaries and startup readiness. Dynamic imports, modules and worker-only programs retain the native worker path.
Provide missing webRequest option enum containers and an event-driven main-frame same-document history fallback.
Normalize Chrome tab ID 0 missing-tab callbacks through the native error scope; preserve valid IDs, Promise rejection and argument validation.

Bridge declared/granted HTTP(S) downloads to the existing native queue with cookies, user agent and Referer; provide owned download IDs, search, cancellation and observed creation/completion/removal events.
Use a dedicated native event port and throttled native observations instead of JavaScript download polling; unload disconnects ports without canceling accepted transfers.

coverage: Generic i18n and tab error semantics
Generic fixture fixed-footer pixels are painted
Reopening has fresh JavaScript document state
Duplicate action request retains the open document
Disabling another extension does not dismiss this popup; disabling the owner does

validation.generic_device_build: Succeeded with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO: /tmp/soulo-catcatch-20261113/completed-device-build.log; no physical-device execution
validation.metadata: export_metadata_json.py --check passed for all 50 locales; version unchanged in this task
validation.source_validation: Current production source passed 44 regression cases plus 2 iPad cases, 0 failures, 0 skips. Early failures are retained in artifacts; corrected native lastError handling, API wrapper lifetime and popup self-sizing/lifecycle rather than relaxing the functional assertions.

limitations: Native extension runtime requires iOS/iPadOS 18.4 or later. No physical-device run in this audit.
This does not certify every Cat Catch feature, arbitrary sites, extension packages or service workers.
Online FFmpeg merging, encrypted-stream workflows, cache/deep capture and full parser/segment-download chains were not verified end to end.
Blob/data download URLs are not implemented by this native download bridge. It supports HTTP(S) GET/POST; advanced Chrome download operations and complete search filters are not implemented.
getDisplayMedia and showSaveFilePicker were undefined in the tested popup runtime.
The generic history fallback reports main-frame same-document changes, not complete subframe history coverage.
Cat Catch hides some advanced injection controls by its own Chrome/Firefox UA version checks; these checks were not rewritten to advertise unverified capabilities.

library_research.recommendation: Continue WKWebExtension + WKWebView with targeted generic API compatibility. No vetted drop-in iOS library found that implements the full Chrome extension runtime.

implementation_scope: Generic bindings, popup host, classic-worker preparation, navigation and downloads apply by API/manifest features rather than Cat Catch name or version. Previously pinned Tampermonkey/TYTY migrations remain narrowly scoped and retain their existing regression coverage.

follow_up.note: The limitations below describe the initial audit; the follow-up supplies later implementation and end-to-end evidence for these items.
